title: Orchestrated dark-launch + canary suite for batching/cache cost recommendations
creator: Lena Zhao
description:
Goal: Implement a safe, automated pathway to evaluate and progressively apply Optimize recommendations (batching and KV-cache profiles) using a dark-launch + canary test harness with operator approval gates and automated rollback triggers. This ticket covers orchestration, telemetry gating, synthetic-traffic validation, approval flow, and playbook for emergency rollback.

Background: Optimize produced actionable config suggestions that can materially reduce token cost but carry regression risk (latency or quality). Existing work focused on staged rollouts and operator latches; this work aims to unify a dark-launch mode that validates suggestions end-to-end against production-like signals before any traffic shift, then a controlled canary activation with metric-based gates and an operator approval checkpoint before wide apply.

Scope and deliverables:
- Dark-launch harness: route a copy of live requests to canary runtime with suggested profile (no user-facing change), collect full telemetry (latency P50/P95, per-route throughput, quality checks, deterministic golden prompts).
- Synthetic traffic runner: reproducible workload generator for spikes and tail-latency stress tests (configurable seeds and sequence lengths).
- Canary activation controller: staged traffic ramp (0->1%->5%->20%) with automated hold/revert on metric regressions and an operator approval step before >20% or global apply.
- Metric gating rules: define signal set (token-cost delta, per-token latency delta, error rate, eval-set quality regression) and thresholds with hysteresis to avoid flapping.
- Rollback automation: automated revert when regression persists for X minutes or X requests, and a fast manual rollback playbook for SREs/ops.
- Observability: per-suggestion dashboard, diff traces (request-level), synthetic vs. production comparisons, and alerting integration (PagerDuty slack) for canary faults.
- Audit trail: record approvals, applied configs, operator comments, and automated decisions to the audit log for Private/Dedicated customers.

Design decisions and trade-offs made so far:
- Dark-launch vs shadowing: We selected dark-launch (request copy with no token billing) to avoid billing noise and preserve customer cost metrics; downside is increased read-only resource usage on canary fleet.
- Thresholds: conservative gating initially (P95 latency +10%, error rate +0.1%, quality regression > 1% on golden prompts) to prioritize correctness over cost; thresholds tunable via release flags.
- Operator approval placement: we require explicit operator approval before increasing canary beyond 20% or pushing to global apply for high-impact suggestions (estimated >10% token cost reduction). This balances autonomy with human-in-the-loop risk control.

Acceptance criteria (minimum):
- Dark-launch pipeline replicates 95% of production request headers and routes to canary without affecting user responses.
- Canary controller enforces ramp percentages and can auto-revert when gating rules are violated in a reproducible test.
- Synthetic runner can simulate 10k requests/min with configurable prompt shapes and produces a report consumed by gating.
- Dashboards show side-by-side metrics and diff timelines; alerts fire when gating thresholds breach.
- Audit entries exist for every auto-apply or manual approval (timestamp, actor, suggestion id, config snapshot).

Telemetry & gating details:
- Signals collected: P50/P95 latency, server-side compute time, token consumption delta, 5xx rate, model-quality metric for golden prompts (BLEU/ROUGE-style surrogate + fingerprint match), user-facing error rate, memory pressure.
- Canary window: evaluate rolling 5m windows with two consecutive windows exceeding threshold to trigger hold/revert.
- Escalation: if automated rollback occurs, open an ops incident and tag the related suggestion id and diffs.

Risks and mitigation:
- Increased canary fleet cost: mitigate with sample-rate and timebox dark-launch windows; reuse low-cost quantized model variants for validation when appropriate.
- False positives on quality regression: include a curated golden set and per-customer evals before apply for PII-sensitive customers.
- Permissioning: audit log and RBAC enforced to prevent unauthorized auto-applies in Private deployments.

Open questions (to resolve before wide rollout):
- What is the default threshold for quality regression across heterogeneous customers? (PM/Research input required)
- Should we charge customers for dark-launch compute in Dedicated? (Billing)
- How to represent the audit record schema for downstream compliance exports? (Security/Compliance)

Next steps / immediate tasks:
1) Wire dark-launch router into proposal pipeline and shard to a canary pod pool (ENG infra task).
2) Implement synthetic runner CLI and CI job with reproducible seeds (ENG test).
3) Build gating rule engine and integrate with alerting (ENG telemetry).
4) UX: expose operator approval button in Console with diff view (PM/Frontend follow-up ticket).
5) Run closed internal pilot on staging with a subset of suggestions and report results in 2 weeks.

Done criteria: all acceptance criteria met, pilot results reviewed, operator playbook approved, and feature toggled for staged rollout to customers.
